agent-workflow: the flow the README tells an agent to follow, exactly as written there.

A project with a few notes in its store. The agent searches, reads the hit, records a verdict,
then uses the output controls from the README block: --expand, --budget, a query that starts
with a dash, an identifier query, and kb context.

  $ kb init --model fake:8
  created location $WORK/proj/.kb
  created store "default" in $WORK/proj (model fake:8)

  $ kb add $WORK/notes/worker.md
  added data/worker.md (3 chunks)

  $ kb add $WORK/notes/reindex.md
  added data/reindex.md (2 chunks)

  $ kb add $WORK/notes/flags.md
  added data/flags.md (2 chunks)

Step 1: search in plain words, as the paste block says, with --json for structured output.

  $ kb search "how do I restart the worker" --caller claude --json
  {
    "search_id": 1,
    "feedback": {
      "useful": "kb feedback 1 RANK --useful",
      "not_useful": "kb feedback 1 RANK --not-useful --note \"why\"",
      "none": "kb feedback 1 --none --note \"why\""
    },
    "query": "how do I restart the worker",
    "mode": "hybrid",
    "hits": [
  ...
  ~ \s+"path": "data/worker.md",
  ...
    ]
  }

Step 2: read the hit with kb show (never the store's files).

  $ kb show data/worker.md
  ---
  title: Restarting the worker
  summary: How to restart the background worker safely.
  tags: [ops]
  updated: 2026-02-01
  ---
  # Restarting the worker

  Drain the queue first, then restart the worker with `systemctl restart kb-worker`.

  ## Rollback

  If the worker does not come back, start the previous release with `systemctl start kb-worker@prev`.

Step 3: say whether it helped, using the command the search printed.

  $ kb feedback --last 1 --useful --caller claude
  recorded: search 1 rank 1 useful=1 (newest search for claude, (time): "how do I restart the worker")

Whole sections instead of chunks, and a size cap.

  $ kb search "restart the worker" --caller claude --mode fts --expand section
  search 2 · 3 hits
  [1] data/worker.md · updated 2026-02-01
  Restarting the worker: How to restart the background worker safely.

  [2] data/worker.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-01
  # Restarting the worker

  Drain the queue first, then restart the worker with `systemctl restart kb-worker`.

  [3] data/worker.md › Rollback · updated 2026-02-01
  If the worker does not come back, start the previous release with `systemctl start kb-worker@prev`.
  search_id=2

  $ kb search "restart the worker" --caller claude --mode fts --budget 60
  search 3 · 3 hits
  [1] data/worker.md · updated 2026-02-01
  How to restart the background worker safely.

  [2] data/worker.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-01

  [3] data/worker.md › Rollback · updated 2026-02-01

  (+3 condensed; raise --budget)
  search_id=3

A query that starts with a dash goes after the flags and --.

  $ kb search --caller claude --json -- --embed-model
  {
    "search_id": 4,
    "feedback": {
      "useful": "kb feedback 4 RANK --useful",
      "not_useful": "kb feedback 4 RANK --not-useful --note \"why\"",
      "none": "kb feedback 4 --none --note \"why\""
    },
    "query": "--embed-model",
    "mode": "hybrid",
    "hits": [
  ...
        "exact_rank": 1,
        "path": "data/flags.md",
  ...
    ]
  }

An identifier matches exactly: the exact list ranks the chunk that says reindex_test.

  $ kb search reindex_test --caller claude --json
  {
    "search_id": 5,
    "feedback": {
      "useful": "kb feedback 5 RANK --useful",
      "not_useful": "kb feedback 5 RANK --not-useful --note \"why\"",
      "none": "kb feedback 5 --none --note \"why\""
    },
    "query": "reindex_test",
    "mode": "hybrid",
    "hits": [
  ...
        "exact_rank": 1,
        "path": "data/reindex.md",
  ...
    ]
  }

kb context prints the hits as Markdown, ready to paste into a prompt.

  $ kb context "restart the worker"
  ## kb context (search 6)

  ### [1] data/worker.md · updated 2026-02-01

  How to restart the background worker safely.

  Restarting the worker: How to restart the background worker safely.

  ### [2] data/worker.md › Rollback · updated 2026-02-01

  How to restart the background worker safely.

  If the worker does not come back, start the previous release with `systemctl start kb-worker@prev`.

  ### [3] data/worker.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-01

  How to restart the background worker safely.

  # Restarting the worker

  Drain the queue first, then restart the worker with `systemctl restart kb-worker`.

  ### [4] data/reindex.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02

  How the reindex_test script checks the index.

  # Reindex test

  Run reindex_test after changing the chunker. A plain reindex test run without the script does
  not compare embeddings.

  ### [5] data/flags.md · updated 2026-02-03

  Command-line flags that choose the embedding model.

  Embedding flags: Command-line flags that choose the embedding model.

  ### [6] data/reindex.md · updated 2026-02-02

  How the reindex_test script checks the index.

  Reindex test: How the reindex_test script checks the index.

  ### [7] data/flags.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-03

  Command-line flags that choose the embedding model.

  # Embedding flags

  Pass --embed-model to choose the model for one run. The default comes from the store config.

  More: kb show data/worker.md
  search 6 · kb feedback 6 RANK --useful or --not-useful

The plain human output, the example at the top of the README's Searching section.

  $ kb search "restart the worker" --caller claude
  search 7 · 7 hits
  [1] data/worker.md · updated 2026-02-01
  Restarting the worker: How to restart the background worker safely.

  [2] data/worker.md › Rollback · updated 2026-02-01
  Restarting the worker › Rollback
  If the worker does not come back, start the previous release with `systemctl start kb-worker@prev`.

  ...
  search_id=7

-- notes/worker.md --
---
title: Restarting the worker
summary: How to restart the background worker safely.
tags: [ops]
updated: 2026-02-01
---
# Restarting the worker

Drain the queue first, then restart the worker with `systemctl restart kb-worker`.

## Rollback

If the worker does not come back, start the previous release with `systemctl start kb-worker@prev`.
-- notes/reindex.md --
---
title: Reindex test
summary: How the reindex_test script checks the index.
tags: [dev]
updated: 2026-02-02
---
# Reindex test

Run reindex_test after changing the chunker. A plain reindex test run without the script does
not compare embeddings.
-- notes/flags.md --
---
title: Embedding flags
summary: Command-line flags that choose the embedding model.
tags: [dev]
updated: 2026-02-03
---
# Embedding flags

Pass --embed-model to choose the model for one run. The default comes from the store config.
